title: Jibril's questions
cue: Jibril asks the Prophet ﷺ about Islam, faith, excellence and the Hour
arabic: عَنْ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ أَيْضًا قَالَ: بَيْنَمَا نَحْنُ جُلُوسٌ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ، إِذْ طَلَعَ عَلَيْنَا رَجُلٌ شَدِيدُ بَيَاضِ الثِّيَابِ، شَدِيدُ سَوَادِ الشَّعْرِ، لَا يُرَى عَلَيْهِ أَثَرُ السَّفَرِ، وَلَا يَعْرِفُهُ مِنَّا أَحَدٌ، حَتَّى جَلَسَ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ، فَأَسْنَدَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ إِلَى رُكْبَتَيْهِ، وَوَضَعَ كَفَّيْهِ عَلَى فَخِذَيْهِ، وَقَالَ: يَا مُحَمَّدُ، أَخْبِرْنِي عَنِ الْإِسْلَامِ. فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: «الْإِسْلَامُ أَنْ تَشْهَدَ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ، وَتُقِيمَ الصَّلَاةَ، وَتُؤْتِيَ الزَّكَاةَ، وَتَصُومَ رَمَضَانَ، وَتَحُجَّ الْبَيْتَ إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا». قَالَ: صَدَقْتَ. فَعَجِبْنَا لَهُ يَسْأَلُهُ وَيُصَدِّقُهُ. قَالَ: فَأَخْبِرْنِي عَنِ الْإِيمَانِ. قَالَ: «أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ، وَتُؤْمِنَ بِالْقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وَشَرِّهِ». قَالَ: صَدَقْتَ. قَالَ: فَأَخْبِرْنِي عَنِ الْإِحْسَانِ. قَالَ: «أَنْ تَعْبُدَ اللَّهَ كَأَنَّكَ تَرَاهُ، فَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ تَرَاهُ فَإِنَّهُ يَرَاكَ». قَالَ: فَأَخْبِرْنِي عَنِ السَّاعَةِ. قَالَ: «مَا الْمَسْئُولُ عَنْهَا بِأَعْلَمَ مِنَ السَّائِلِ». قَالَ: فَأَخْبِرْنِي عَنْ أَمَارَاتِهَا. قَالَ: «أَنْ تَلِدَ الْأَمَةُ رَبَّتَهَا، وَأَنْ تَرَى الْحُفَاةَ الْعُرَاةَ الْعَالَةَ رِعَاءَ الشَّاءِ يَتَطَاوَلُونَ فِي الْبُنْيَانِ». ثُمَّ انْطَلَقَ، فَلَبِثْتُ مَلِيًّا، ثُمَّ قَالَ: «يَا عُمَرُ، أَتَدْرِي مَنِ السَّائِلُ؟». قُلْتُ: اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ. قَالَ: «فَإِنَّهُ جِبْرِيلُ أَتَاكُمْ يُعَلِّمُكُمْ دِينَكُمْ».
translation:
It is also narrated from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: One day, while we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a man came upon us whose clothes were intensely white and whose hair was intensely black. No trace of travel could be seen on him, and none of us knew him.

He sat down by the Prophet ﷺ, rested his knees against his knees, placed his palms on his thighs, and said: “Muhammad, tell me about Islam.”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Islam is that you bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, that you establish the prayer, give the [[zakat]], fast Ramadan, and make pilgrimage to the House if you are able to find a way there.” He said: “You have spoken truly.” We were amazed at him: he asks him, then confirms what he says.

He said: “Then tell me about faith.” He said: “That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers and the Last Day, and that you believe in the decree, its good and its bad.” He said: “You have spoken truly.”

He said: “Then tell me about [[ihsan]].” He said: “That you worship Allah as though you see Him; and if you do not see Him, He sees you.”

He said: “Then tell me about the Hour.” He said: “The one asked about it knows no more of it than the one asking.”

He said: “Then tell me about its signs.” He said: “That the slave woman gives birth to her mistress, and that you see the barefoot, the unclothed, the destitute, the shepherds of sheep, competing in raising tall buildings.”

Then he went away, and I stayed a long while. Then he said: “Umar, do you know who the questioner was?” I said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “That was Jibril. He came to you to teach you your religion.”

provenance.note: Hashes are of each witness's text of this narration, from al-Nawawi's opening words to the end before his attribution line, with honorific formulas written as we print them (ﷺ, رضي الله عنه): see data-sources/hadith-arabic/SOURCE.md. Ibn Daqiq and hadith-api agree with ours. al-Haytami's print lacks جلوس, adds قال before فعجبنا, writes المسؤول for المسئول, and reads أمارتها and فلبث; ours follows the other two at each point.

notes.text: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id calls this a great [[hadith]] that takes in every outward and inward duty, and says the knowledge of the law all goes back to it, so that it is like a mother of the [[sunnah]], as al-Fatihah is called the mother of the Quran.

source.work: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id, Sharh al-Arba'in al-Nawawiyya
